title: Coast Guard Medevacs Injured Salor
description: B-roll of the U.S. Coast Guard transporting and providing medical care to a patient from a Navy warship who received a head injury. Produced by Petty Officer 2nd Class Jetta H. Disco.

transcript.text: My name is DM1 Michael W. Tapp, the Officer in Charge and Coast Guard, ACE and Navigation
We were deploying a working-aids navigation on why doing 0.2 in San Diego Bay when we were
on our way to another mission.
We heard that the stress call could come from Navy Force at 6'9", at which point we diverted
to 6'9", and that transporting of patient movement that struck in the head, received a head injury
while attempting to anchor to a foreign ball.
We transported the patient from the US Navy to the Coast Guard War, ACE here in San Diego.
We had a Navy corpsman with us, we transported with the patient as well.
He was already on a stretcher when we received him.
We just monitored life signs and brought him strength in place.
He was in and out of consciousness at the time we received him.
He was conscious with slide in and out during the transport.
The Coast Guard boat crew did an excellent job of quickly switching from one mission,
so it was A-time, which is obviously a non-emergency situation, right into an emergency situation
where they were able to provide assistance to the US Navy and safely save life.
